instructions: Lie on your back with straight legs spread wide and the free arm extended on the floor.
Hold a kettlebell beside one shoulder with the elbow bent.
Press the bell upward while turning slightly toward the opposite side and lifting the working shoulder.
Reverse the torso turn as you lower the bell, returning the upper arm toward the floor.
Keep the movement controlled and change arms after the set.
description: A small torso roll accompanies this one-arm floor press, allowing the loaded shoulder to move through a larger range.
aliases: Kettlebell Extended Range One Arm Press on Floor

name: Kettlebell Figure 8
instructions: Stand with feet wider than hip-width and hold a kettlebell in one hand.
Bend your knees and lean forward from your hips while keeping your back steady.
Pass the bell between your legs and receive it behind one thigh with the other hand.
Bring it around the outside of that leg and pass it between the legs again to the first hand.
Continue a smooth figure-eight path while keeping your feet planted.
description: Passing one kettlebell around and between the legs challenges grip, coordination and trunk control.

name: Double-Kettlebell Front Squat
instructions: Hold one kettlebell at each shoulder with elbows close to your torso.
Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart and toes turned slightly outward.
Bend your hips and knees to squat down, keeping your heels planted and chest lifted.
Push through your feet to return upright.
Keep the bells supported at the shoulders throughout.
description: Two kettlebells stay at the shoulders during a squat that works the quadriceps and glutes.

name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
instructions: Hold a kettlebell by the sides of its handle close to your chest.
Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart and toes slightly outward.
Bend your knees and hips to lower between your legs while keeping your feet planted.
Keep your knees aligned with your toes and stop at a controlled depth.
Push through both feet to stand upright.
description: A kettlebell held close to the chest provides front loading during a squat for the quadriceps and glutes.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Hang Clean
instructions: Hold a kettlebell in one hand with feet apart.
Push your hips back and lean forward, letting the bell swing between your legs.
Drive your hips forward to bring the bell upward close to your body.
Guide your hand through the handle and catch the bell softly against your forearm at the shoulder.
Lower into the next backswing with control.
Complete the set before changing arms.
description: Hip drive lifts one kettlebell from between the legs to rest against the forearm at the shoulder.

name: Kettlebell Lunge with Under-Leg Pass
instructions: Stand holding one kettlebell at your side.
Step forward with the leg opposite the loaded hand and bend both knees into a lunge.
Pass the kettlebell beneath the front thigh to your other hand.
Push through the front foot to return to standing with the bell now on the other side.
Repeat with the opposite leg and continue alternating.
description: A kettlebell transfers between the hands beneath the front thigh during a lunge, working the legs and coordination.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Clean and Jerk
instructions: Hold a kettlebell in one hand, bend your knees and push your hips back, then drive upward to bring it to your shoulder.
Settle the bell against the forearm with your elbow under it.
Dip both knees and drive through your legs to send the bell upward.
Bend your knees again to move under the bell as your arm straightens overhead.
Stand upright to finish the catch.
Lower to the shoulder and then beside your body under control. Change arms after the set.
description: A clean brings the kettlebell to the shoulder before a separate leg drive and bent-knee catch send it overhead.
aliases: Kettlebell One Arm Clean and Jerk

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Floor Press with Legs Extended
instructions: Lie on your back with both legs straight and your free hand resting on your abdomen.
Hold a kettlebell beside your chest with your working upper arm resting lightly on the floor.
Press the kettlebell above your chest until your arm is straight.
Lower slowly until the upper arm touches the floor gently.
Complete the set before changing arms.
description: A one-arm press from the floor trains the chest and triceps with the legs extended and the free hand resting on the abdomen.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Overhead Partial Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet apart and hold a kettlebell overhead in one straight arm.
Keep the weight steady above your shoulder while bending your hips and knees into a shallow squat.
Keep both feet planted and your torso upright.
Push through both feet to stand again, keeping the arm extended overhead.
Lower the kettlebell under control after the set, then repeat holding it in the other hand.
description: A shallow two-leg squat is performed while one kettlebell stays overhead, working the quadriceps and glutes while the shoulder and trunk steady the load.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Overhead Press
instructions: Stand with a kettlebell held at one shoulder and palm angled inward.
Keep your legs still and press the bell upward, allowing the elbow to move outward.
Finish with your arm straight overhead without leaning your torso back.
Lower the bell slowly to shoulder height.
Repeat, then change arms.
description: Pressing one kettlebell overhead with the elbow moving outward trains the shoulder and triceps.
aliases: Kettlebell One Arm Military Press to the Side

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Push Press
instructions: Stand with a kettlebell at one shoulder and elbow below the handle.
Bend your knees slightly while keeping your torso upright.
Extend your legs firmly and continue the drive by pressing the kettlebell overhead.
Finish with the arm and legs straight.
Lower the bell to the shoulder with control, then repeat and change sides.
description: A shallow leg dip supplies momentum for a one-arm overhead press that works the shoulders, triceps and legs.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Row
instructions: Hold a kettlebell in one hand, place the opposite foot forward and lean forward from your hips with your knees slightly bent.
Rest your free hand on your front thigh and keep your back steady as the loaded arm hangs beneath your shoulder.
Pull the bell toward your lower ribs with the elbow close to your torso.
Lower until your arm extends without twisting your body.
Complete the set, then change arms.
description: One kettlebell rows toward the ribs while the torso stays leaning forward and the free hand supports it on the front thigh, training the upper back and lats.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Snatch
instructions: Hold a kettlebell in one hand, bend your knees slightly and push your hips back to swing it between your legs.
Drive your hips forward to accelerate the bell upward close to your body.
Guide your hand through the handle as your arm straightens overhead, letting the bell settle against your forearm.
Lower with control into the next backswing.
Finish the set, then change arms.
description: Hip drive carries one kettlebell from between the legs to overhead in a continuous lift, working the glutes and hamstrings while the shoulder controls the weight.

name: Two-Hand Kettlebell Diagonal Raise
instructions: Stand with feet apart and hold one kettlebell in both hands low in front of one hip.
Keep your elbows nearly straight as you lift the bell diagonally across your torso.
Raise it above the opposite shoulder while allowing a small upper-body turn.
Lower along the same diagonal with control.
Complete the set and repeat toward the other side.
description: Both hands guide one kettlebell from a low position across the body to a high diagonal, working the shoulders and trunk control.

name: Kettlebell Pistol Squat
instructions: Hold a kettlebell close to your chest with both hands.
Balance on one foot and extend the other leg forward.
Bend your supporting knee and hip to lower into a controlled single-leg squat, keeping the heel planted.
Push through the supporting foot to stand while keeping the free foot clear.
Complete the set before changing legs.
description: Holding a kettlebell at the chest adds load to a single-leg squat with the free leg extended forward.

name: Alternating Plyometric Push-Up over Kettlebell
instructions: Set one stable kettlebell on the floor and start in a plank with one hand on its handle and the other on the floor.
Bend both elbows to lower your chest.
Push forcefully and shift your body across the kettlebell, exchanging hand positions.
Land with the opposite hand on the handle and the other on the floor, bending your elbows to absorb the change.
Continue controlled side changes while keeping your body aligned.
description: An explosive uneven push-up switches which hand rests on a single kettlebell, training the chest and arms.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Press Seated on Floor
instructions: Sit on the floor with legs straight and spread apart.
Hold a kettlebell beside one shoulder with your palm facing forward and keep your torso upright.
Press it overhead until your arm is straight.
Lower slowly to the shoulder without leaning backward.
Complete the set, then change arms.
description: A one-arm overhead press from a straddle sit works the shoulder and triceps without help from the legs.

name: Seated Double-Kettlebell Overhead Press
instructions: Sit tall on a flat bench with your feet planted.
Hold a kettlebell beside each shoulder with palms facing forward.
Press both bells overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly to shoulder level while keeping your torso steady.
description: Two kettlebells press overhead together while sitting upright on a flat bench, training the shoulders and triceps.
aliases: Kettlebell Seated Two Arm Military Press

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Overhead Press with Side Lean
instructions: Stand with one kettlebell at each shoulder.
Press one bell overhead while leaning your torso slightly toward the opposite side and looking toward the raised weight.
Keep the other bell at its shoulder and both feet planted.
Return your torso upright as you lower the bell to shoulder height.
Complete the repetitions, then change arms, keeping the side lean controlled and avoiding a backward arch.
description: One kettlebell presses overhead with a small sideways torso lean while the other remains at the shoulder, working the shoulders and triceps with trunk control.
aliases: Alternating Kettlebell Overhead Press with Side Lean

name: Kettlebell Sumo High Pull
instructions: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width and toes angled outward.
Hold one kettlebell with both hands between your legs and bend your knees and hips.
Drive upward through your legs, then pull the bell toward your upper chest.
Let your elbows rise outward above your hands while keeping the bell close.
Lower the bell and bend your hips and knees to reset.
description: A wide-stance hip and leg drive lifts the kettlebell into a high pull with elbows traveling outward.

name: Two-Hand Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Stand with feet apart and hold the kettlebell handle in both hands.
Bend your knees slightly and push your hips back, letting the bell swing between your legs.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall and let the bell float up toward chest height.
Keep your arms relaxed enough that the hips supply the lift.
Guide the bell back between your legs as you push your hips back for the next swing.
Finish by controlling the bell down rather than abruptly stopping it in front of you.
description: Hip extension swings a kettlebell from between the legs to about chest height, emphasizing the glutes and hamstrings.

name: Double-Kettlebell Thruster
instructions: Hold one kettlebell at each shoulder with feet about shoulder-width apart.
Lower into a squat while keeping the bells close and your chest lifted.
Drive through your feet to rise and carry that momentum into an overhead press.
Finish standing with both arms straight.
Lower the kettlebells to your shoulders and begin the next controlled squat.
description: A front squat flows directly into a two-arm overhead press, combining leg drive with shoulder and triceps work.

name: Kettlebell Turkish Get-Up
instructions: Lie on your back with the kettlebell held above one shoulder and that same-side knee bent with its foot planted. Extend the opposite leg.
Roll onto the opposite forearm, then press onto that hand while keeping the loaded arm vertical.
Lift your hips enough to sweep the extended leg underneath you, placing its knee on the floor.
Bring your torso upright into a half-kneeling position and move the support hand off the floor.
Push through the front foot to stand, keeping the kettlebell steady overhead.
Reverse the sequence through half-kneeling, hand support, leg sweep and forearm support to lie down.
Lower the kettlebell safely before changing sides.
description: This floor-to-standing sequence keeps a kettlebell supported overhead through a roll, hand support, leg sweep and half-kneeling rise.

name: Double-Kettlebell Clean
instructions: Stand with feet apart holding one kettlebell in each hand.
Push your hips back and lean forward, guiding the bells between your legs.
Drive your hips forward to bring the bells upward close to your torso.
Bring your hands through the handles so each bell settles against its forearm at shoulder level.
Lower both bells with control into the next backswing.
description: Both kettlebells rise from between the legs to rest against the forearms at the shoulders using coordinated hip and leg drive.

name: Standing Double-Kettlebell Overhead Press
instructions: Stand with feet apart and a kettlebell supported beside each shoulder.
Gently tighten your abdomen and keep your knees still.
Press both kettlebells overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower with control to shoulder level.
description: Both arms press together from the shoulders to overhead while the legs remain still.

name: Double-Kettlebell Bent-Over Row
instructions: Hold a kettlebell in each hand, bend your knees slightly and lean forward from your hips.
Let your arms extend below your shoulders while keeping your back steady.
Pull both bells toward your lower ribs with elbows close to your sides.
Draw your shoulder blades together without lifting your torso.
Lower the weights until your arms extend.
description: Both kettlebells move together toward the ribs while the torso stays in a steady forward lean.

name: Kettlebell Windmill
instructions: Stand with a kettlebell overhead in one straight arm and feet turned slightly away from that side.
Shift your hips back toward the loaded side and incline your torso toward the opposite leg.
Slide your free hand down toward that foot while keeping the loaded arm vertical.
Keep your eyes on the bell and stop at a controlled depth.
Return upright through the hips, then repeat and change sides.
description: An overhead kettlebell stays above the shoulder while the hips move back and the torso bends and turns toward the opposite foot.

name: Wall Sit with Alternating Leg Extension
instructions: Place your back against a wall and slide down into a seated position with feet planted forward.
Extend your arms to the sides and keep your back against the wall.
Straighten one knee to lift that foot forward while the other foot stays planted.
Lower it and straighten the opposite leg.
Continue alternating without changing the height of your hips.
description: One leg straightens at a time while the other supports a wall sit, emphasizing the quadriceps.

name: Bent-Knee Front Lever Raise on Rings
instructions: Hang from secure rings with your arms nearly straight and both knees bent.
Tighten your abdomen and glutes to keep your torso and thighs aligned.
Pull down through the rings and lean backward, raising your hips until your torso and thighs are approximately horizontal.
Keep your knees bent and your arms nearly straight as you lower back to the hanging position.
Repeat with control, without kicking your legs.
description: The torso and thighs rise together from a ring hang into a bent-knee front lever. The back muscles pull through the shoulders while the abdomen and glutes keep the body aligned.

name: Knee-Reach Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet planted.
Extend both arms toward your thighs.
Curl your shoulders upward while reaching both hands toward your knees.
Keep your neck relaxed and your feet on the floor.
Lower your upper back slowly.
description: Both hands slide toward the knees as the upper back curls off the floor, training the abdominals.

name: Barbell Kneeling Jump to Squat
instructions: Start kneeling with a barbell held securely across your upper back and both hands on the bar.
Sit your hips back slightly, then drive your hips forward and upward.
Pull your feet beneath you to land in a balanced crouched squat.
Keep your chest lifted and control the bar on your shoulders.
Return carefully to the kneeling start before repeating.
description: An explosive hip drive moves the body from kneeling onto the feet into a crouched squat while a barbell rests on the upper back.

name: Kneeling Single-Arm Lat Stretch
instructions: Start on your hands and knees with your hips above your knees.
Reach one arm forward and lower that forearm toward the floor.
Bend the other arm beneath your chest for support as you lower your chest toward the floor.
Keep your hips above your knees and pause at a gentle stretch along the side of your back.
Press back to the starting position, then change arms.
description: One arm reaches forward while the other bends beneath the chest. The hips stay above the knees as the chest lowers to stretch the reaching side of the back.

name: Kneeling Forearm Plank with Shoulder Taps
instructions: Place your knees and forearms on the floor with elbows beneath your shoulders.
Keep a straight line from shoulders through hips to knees.
Lift one hand and forearm to touch the opposite shoulder while the other forearm stays down.
Return that forearm to the floor and tap with the other hand.
Continue alternating without twisting your hips.
description: Alternating shoulder taps from a knee-supported forearm plank challenge abdominal control as each supporting arm takes more load.

name: Kneeling Push-Up
instructions: Place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and keep both knees on the floor.
Move your hips forward until your body forms a straight line from knees to head.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms.
Keep your knees down and your hips aligned throughout.
description: A push-up with the knees supported works the chest, triceps and shoulders through a shorter body lever.

name: Forward-Leaning Parallel-Bar Dip
instructions: Support yourself above parallel bars with your arms straight and your feet clear of the floor.
Keep your legs together and lean your torso forward as you bend your elbows.
Lower between the bars through a comfortable shoulder range, allowing your straight legs to trail slightly behind you.
Press through the bars to straighten your arms and return your torso upright.
Keep the movement controlled and your feet off the floor throughout.
description: Lean your torso forward as you lower between parallel bars, keeping your legs together and slightly behind you. The chest and triceps press your body back to the top.

name: L-Sit Chin-Up
instructions: Grip a secure bar with palms facing toward you and arms extended.
Raise both straight legs in front of you until they are approximately horizontal.
Hold that L position while pulling your torso upward toward the bar.
Lower slowly until your arms extend, keeping the legs raised.
Lower your legs under control when the set is complete.
description: A chin-up is performed while both legs stay extended forward at hip height, adding abdominal and hip-flexor work.

name: Floor L-Sit Hold
instructions: Sit with legs straight and together, placing your palms beside your hips.
Press down through your hands to lift your hips clear of the floor.
Keep your knees straight and raise your heels so the legs stay horizontal in front of you.
Hold with your shoulders pressed down and elbows straight.
Lower your hips and heels with control.
description: Straight arms support the hips and legs above the floor while the abdominals and hip flexors maintain the L shape.

name: Low Landmine Rotation
instructions: Secure one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment.
Stand facing the free end and hold it with both hands near hip height.
Pivot your feet and turn your hips and torso to move the bar end toward one side.
Rotate through the center toward the other side, keeping the hand path low.
Control the bar through each change of direction.
description: The free end of an anchored bar moves side to side near hip height while the feet pivot and the torso rotates.

name: Single-Arm Landmine Lateral Raise
instructions: Secure one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment and stand beside the free end.
Hold the free end with one hand low across the front of the opposite hip.
Keep a small, steady elbow bend and raise the bar end outward toward the working side.
Continue until your hand is above shoulder height within a comfortable range, without leaning your torso.
Lower through the same arc with control.
Complete the set before changing arms.
description: The free bar end travels from across the hips upward and outward in a shoulder-raising arc.

name: Planche Lean Hold
instructions: Start in a straight-arm plank with hands planted and legs together.
Keep your elbows straight and press the floor away through your shoulders.
Shift your body forward until your shoulders are ahead of your hands, keeping your toes on the floor.
Hold that position with your abdomen and glutes tightened.
Shift back under control to release the hold.
description: Leaning the shoulders ahead of the hands increases upper-body loading while the toes remain on the floor.

name: Left Hook Shadowboxing
instructions: Stand in a boxing stance with your left foot forward, knees soft and both hands near your face.
Turn through your hips and torso while pivoting on the ball of the left foot.
Sweep your bent left arm across at shoulder height, keeping the elbow bent and wrist aligned with the fist.
Keep your right hand near your chin.
Return the left hand to guard and reset your stance.
description: A bent left arm sweeps horizontally as the hips and torso turn, practicing a boxing hook without impact.

name: Lying Bench Knee Tuck and Leg Extension
instructions: Lie on your back along a flat bench and place your palms on the pad beside your hips.
Lift both legs with knees bent and draw them toward your torso.
Extend your legs outward over the end of the bench while keeping your back controlled against the pad.
Bend your knees to draw them back in, allowing a small pelvic curl at the top.
Keep the movement smooth without swinging.
description: From a lying bench position, the knees draw inward and then extend away to train the abs and hip flexors.

name: Lying Hamstring Stretch with Knee Extension
instructions: Lie on your back with one leg extended on the floor.
Lift the other thigh toward your torso and hold behind it with both hands.
Slowly straighten the raised knee until you feel a comfortable stretch in the back of the thigh.
Bend the knee slightly to release while keeping the thigh supported.
Repeat gently, then change legs.
description: The hands hold one thigh raised while the knee extends to stretch the hamstrings.

name: Alternating Machine Leg Press
instructions: Adjust the seat and sit with your back supported, placing one foot on each platform.
Hold the handles and keep both feet centered on their platforms.
Press one platform away until that leg is nearly straight.
Bend the knee slowly to return, then press with the other leg.
Continue alternating while keeping your pelvis against the seat.
description: Independent foot platforms let each leg press in turn to train the quadriceps and glutes.

name: Alternating Neutral-Grip Machine Row
instructions: Adjust the seat so your chest rests against the pad and both feet are supported.
Hold the close handles with palms facing each other.
Pull one handle toward your ribs, keeping the elbow close to your torso.
Return it slowly while keeping your chest on the pad.
Repeat with the other arm and continue alternating.
description: Independent handles are pulled alternately toward the torso while a chest pad supports the body.
aliases: Lever Alternating Narrow Grip Seated Row

name: Machine-Assisted Pull-Up
instructions: Select the assistance level and hold the overhead handles with palms facing away from you.
Place both knees on the moving assistance pad and let your arms lengthen.
Draw your elbows down and pull your upper chest toward the handles without swinging.
Lower slowly until your arms are long again, keeping both knees on the pad.
description: An assisted pull-up uses a moving knee pad to reduce the body weight lifted while the lats and biceps pull the body upward.

name: Seated Machine Back Extension
instructions: Sit on the machine with your lower legs against its support pads and the moving pad against your upper back.
Adjust the machine so your hips stay supported as your torso moves.
Lean forward under control through a comfortable range.
Press your upper back into the pad to bring your torso upright, without throwing your head back.
Return forward slowly while keeping your hips in the seat.
description: This seated back extension moves the torso against a padded lever to work the muscles of the lower back.

name: Landmine Bent-Over Row
instructions: Secure one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment and straddle the bar facing the loaded end.
Bend at your hips and knees, then take the close two-hand grip just behind the plates.
Keep your torso steady and pull the loaded end toward your lower chest.
Lower the bar slowly until your arms are long, keeping the same forward lean.
description: A close-grip landmine row pulls the anchored bar toward the torso, working the upper back and lats while the legs support a bent-over stance.

name: Landmine Row with V-Bar
instructions: Secure the bar in its pivot and place the V-bar handle beneath the loaded end.
Straddle the bar, bend your knees and lean forward from your hips to take both handles with palms facing each other.
Hold your torso still as you draw your elbows back and pull the handle toward your abdomen.
Lower the weight under control without rounding your back.
description: This bent-over landmine row uses a V-bar handle for a close grip, working the lats and upper back.

name: Seated Machine High-Arm Biceps Curl
instructions: Sit upright and adjust the seat so your upper arms rest on the raised pads near shoulder height.
Hold the handles with your palms facing up and keep your upper arms supported.
Bend your elbows to curl the handles toward your head without lifting your arms off the pads.
Lower the handles slowly until your elbows are nearly straight.
description: The upper arms rest on raised machine pads while the elbows curl the handles toward the shoulders. The biceps work against the machine resistance.

name: Seated Machine Calf Press
instructions: Sit against the backrest and place the balls of your feet on the footplate with your heels free to move.
Set the seat distance so your knees stay slightly bent, then hold the side handles.
Push through the balls of your feet to point your toes away and move the footplate.
Let your ankles bend back slowly while keeping the knee angle nearly unchanged.
description: A seated calf press moves the footplate through the ankles while the legs remain nearly straight, targeting the calves.

name: Seated Machine Chest Press
instructions: Sit with your back against the pad and your feet planted.
Adjust the seat so the handles are near chest height and take the forward-facing handles.
Press the handles away from your chest while keeping your back supported.
Bend your elbows slowly to bring the handles back without letting the weight drop.
description: This seated chest press uses a weight-stack machine to work the chest, with help from the shoulders and triceps.

name: Plate-Loaded Seated Chest Press
instructions: Sit on the machine with your back against its pad and your feet firmly planted.
Take the handles beside your chest with palms facing forward.
Press both handles forward until your arms are long, keeping your shoulders against the pad.
Return the handles slowly to the starting position.
description: The plate-loaded seated chest press moves two lever arms forward to work the chest, shoulders and triceps.

name: Standing Lever Deadlift
instructions: Stand between the machine handles with your feet about hip-width apart.
Bend at your hips and knees to grip the handles beside your legs.
Keep your back steady and push through your feet to stand, extending your hips and knees together.
Finish upright without leaning backward.
Bend your hips and knees to lower the levers under control.
description: The standing lever deadlift lifts the machine handles from beside the legs, working the glutes and thighs.

name: Plate-Loaded Decline Chest Press
instructions: Sit in the machine with your back supported and feet on the floor.
Take the handles beside your lower chest and keep your shoulders against the pad.
Press forward and slightly downward along the machine path until your arms are long.
Return slowly until the handles reach the starting position.
description: This seated machine press directs the handles forward and downward to work the chest, with assistance from the triceps and shoulders.

name: Machine Donkey Calf Raise
instructions: Place the balls of both feet on the machine platform with your heels free.
Bend forward at your hips, place the load pad over your hips and support your upper body on the front pads.
Keep your legs nearly straight and raise your heels by pushing through the balls of your feet.
Lower your heels slowly through a comfortable ankle range without changing your torso position.
description: A machine donkey calf raise loads the hips while the torso bends forward, allowing the calves to raise and lower the heels.

name: Machine Front Pulldown
instructions: Sit beneath the handles with your thighs held under the pads and feet planted.
Take the overhead handles with palms facing forward.
Keep your torso steady as you draw your elbows down beside your body and bring the handles toward your upper chest.
Allow your arms to lengthen slowly as the handles return overhead.
description: The machine front pulldown draws overhead handles down in front of the body, working the lats and elbow flexors.

name: Machine Gripless Shrug
instructions: Stand under the shoulder pads with your feet on the platform.
Set the pad height so you can stand tall, with elbows bent and hands resting on the supports.
Lift your shoulders straight toward your ears to raise the pads.
Lower your shoulders slowly without rolling them or bending your knees.
description: A gripless machine shrug places resistance directly on the shoulders to work the upper trapezius.

name: Machine Shoulder-Pad Shrug
instructions: Position your shoulders beneath the machine pads and stand upright on the platform.
Keep your elbows bent and rest your hands on the machine supports.
Raise the pads by lifting both shoulders toward your ears while keeping your arms and legs still.
Lower your shoulders gently to the starting position.
description: This shoulder-pad shrug raises the machine load through shoulder elevation rather than through a hand-held weight, targeting the trapezius.

name: Seated Machine Grip Squeeze
instructions: Sit beside the grip machine with both feet planted and your arms reaching down to its handles.
Wrap your fingers around the moving grip bar and keep your wrists steady.
Close your hands to squeeze the bars together and lift the lever.
Open your fingers slowly to lower the lever while retaining contact with the handles.
description: A seated grip machine provides resistance as the fingers close, working the forearm muscles used for gripping.

name: Machine Hammer-Grip Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit with your upper arms resting on the front pad and your feet on the floor.
Take the handles with palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows to bring the handles toward your shoulders while keeping your upper arms on the pad.
Lower the handles slowly until your arms are nearly straight.
description: The hammer-grip preacher curl supports the upper arms while the elbows bend, working the biceps and other elbow flexors with a neutral grip.

name: Plate-Loaded High Row
instructions: Sit facing the machine with your chest on the support pad and feet on the supports.
Take the overhead-forward handles with palms facing down.
Pull your elbows down and back to bring the handles toward your ribs, keeping your chest on the pad.
Let the handles travel forward and upward slowly as your arms lengthen.
description: The supported high row pulls from above and in front of the body to work the upper back and lats.

name: Prone-Supported Machine Single-Leg Hip Extension
instructions: Lie face down across the machine support and hold its handles.
Place one foot against the moving footplate with that knee bent, keeping the other leg supported.
Push the working leg backward by extending the hip, keeping your pelvis on the pad.
Bring the knee forward under control to the start.
Complete the movement with the other leg using the same setup.
description: This prone-supported hip extension drives one leg backward against a machine lever, working the glutes and hamstrings.

name: Single-Leg Horizontal Machine Leg Press
instructions: Sit with your back and hips against the pads.
Place one foot on the footplate and keep the other foot off the footplate, resting on the machine support.
Hold the handles and push through the working foot to extend that knee and hip.
Bend the working leg slowly until you return to the start without lifting your pelvis.
Switch legs after completing the intended repetitions.
description: The horizontal single-leg press slides the seat away from a fixed footplate as one leg extends. The quadriceps and glutes work while the pads support the torso.

name: Plate-Loaded Incline Chest Press
instructions: Sit with your back against the angled machine pad and both feet planted.
Grip the handles beside your upper chest, with palms facing forward.
Press the handles forward and upward along their path without lifting your back from the pad.
Return slowly until the handles are beside your chest.
description: This plate-loaded machine press follows an upward path to work the chest, with the front shoulders and triceps assisting.

name: Incline Machine Chest Press with Foot Supports
instructions: Sit against the angled back pad with both feet on the machine supports.
Grip the handles beside your upper chest and keep your shoulders supported.
Press the handles upward and forward until your arms are long.
Bend your elbows slowly to return without lifting your back from the pad.
description: This incline machine press supports the back and feet while the chest, shoulders and triceps press the handles upward.

name: Kneeling Single-Leg Machine Curl
instructions: Place one knee on the support pad and lean forward with your forearms resting on the front pad.
Position the back of the working ankle beneath the moving roller.
Bend the working knee to bring your heel toward your buttocks, keeping the thigh and pelvis steady.
Lower the roller slowly until the working leg is nearly straight.
Switch the supported and working legs to train the other side.
description: The kneeling machine curl supports one knee while the other leg bends against a roller, targeting the hamstrings.

name: Kneeling Machine Lower-Body Twist
instructions: Kneel on the rotating pads and hold the upper handles with your upper arms against the front supports.
Keep your chest facing the machine and gently tighten your abdomen.
Turn your knees and pelvis together toward one side against the resistance.
Return to the middle under control without pulling your shoulders around.
Complete the set, then adjust the starting direction to train the other side.
description: This kneeling rotary machine turns the lower body beneath a supported upper body to work the obliques.

name: Seated Machine Lateral Raise
instructions: Sit upright with your back supported and your upper arms against the side pads.
Hold the handles with elbows bent and feet planted.
Lift your elbows outward to raise the pads until your upper arms approach shoulder height.
Lower the pads slowly, keeping your elbows bent and torso still.
description: A machine lateral raise lifts bent arms out to the sides against padded levers, targeting the side of the shoulders.

name: Seated Machine Leg Extension
instructions: Sit against the back pad with your knees aligned with the machine pivot.
Place the roller across the front of your lower legs just above the ankles and hold the side handles.
Straighten both knees to lift the roller, keeping your hips in the seat.
Bend your knees slowly to lower the roller to the starting position.
description: The seated leg extension straightens the knees against a padded roller to work the quadriceps.

name: Lying Machine Leg Curl
instructions: Lie face down with your knees near the edge of the support pad and the roller behind your lower legs, just above the heels.
Hold the handles and keep your hips against the pad.
Bend both knees to curl your heels toward your buttocks without lifting your hips.
Lower the roller slowly until your legs are nearly straight.
description: The lying machine leg curl bends both knees against resistance to work the hamstrings, with the calves assisting.

name: Lying Machine Leg Curl, Two Legs Up and One Leg Down
instructions: Lie face down on the leg-curl machine with the roller behind both lower legs and hold the handles.
Curl the roller upward using both legs while keeping your hips on the pad.
Keep one leg against the roller and move the other clear of it.
Lower the roller slowly using only the working leg.
Bring both legs back under the roller and repeat, changing the lowering leg for the other side.
description: This leg curl raises the load with both legs and lowers it with one, increasing the lowering demand on the working hamstrings.

name: Plate-Loaded Seated Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit with your back against the pad and both feet planted.
Take the handles at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
Press both handles upward while keeping your torso supported.
Lower the handles slowly back to shoulder height without letting the plates drop.
description: The seated shoulder press moves plate-loaded levers overhead, working the shoulders and triceps.

name: Close-Grip Machine Seated Row
instructions: Sit facing the machine with your chest against its support and feet planted.
Hold the close handles with palms facing each other and arms reaching forward.
Pull your elbows back beside your ribs to bring the handles toward your abdomen.
Return slowly as your arms lengthen, keeping your chest on the pad.
description: This close-grip seated row uses a chest support while the upper back and lats pull the handles toward the body.

name: Single-Arm Landmine Row with Thigh Support
instructions: Secure one end of the bar in a landmine attachment and stand beside the loaded end.
Bend your knees and lean forward from your hips, holding the bar behind the plates with one hand and resting the other hand on your thigh.
Keep your torso steady as you pull that elbow back and bring the loaded end toward your ribs.
Lower the bar slowly until the working arm is long.
Repeat with the other arm from the opposite side of the bar.
description: The single-arm landmine row draws an anchored bar toward one side of the torso, working the lats and upper back.
aliases: Lever One Arm Bent over Row

name: Single-Arm Plate-Loaded High Row
instructions: Sit facing the machine with your chest on the pad and feet on the supports.
Hold one overhead-forward handle while the other hand steadies you on the machine.
Draw the working elbow down and back to bring the handle beside your ribs.
Let the arm lengthen slowly without turning your torso.
Switch arms and use the same controlled movement.
description: The single-arm high row pulls one lever down and back while the chest stays supported, working the upper back and lats.
aliases: Lever One Arm Lateral High Row

name: Single-Arm Wide Machine Pulldown
instructions: Sit beneath the wide handles with your thighs under the pads and feet planted.
Grasp one overhead handle with the working hand and hold the machine support with the other.
Draw the working elbow down toward your side, bringing the handle toward your shoulder.
Return the handle overhead slowly without leaning sideways.
Repeat with the other arm.
description: This wide machine pulldown trains one side at a time as the lats draw the arm down from overhead.
aliases: Lever One Arm Lateral Wide Pulldown

name: Standing Single-Arm Angled Lever Press
instructions: Stand facing the pivoted lever and hold its handle in one hand beside your shoulder.
Plant both feet and gently tighten your abdomen to keep your torso steady.
Press the handle upward and forward along the lever arc until your arm is long.
Bend your elbow slowly to return the handle toward your shoulder.
Complete the movement with the other arm.
description: The standing angled lever press pushes one handle upward and forward on a pivoted apparatus, working the shoulders and triceps.

name: Seated Machine Dip with Overhand Grip
instructions: Sit on the dip machine with your thighs beneath its restraint pad and both feet planted, then lean slightly forward.
Take the handles beside your hips with palms facing down.
Push the handles downward by straightening your elbows, keeping your body in the seat.
Allow the handles to rise slowly as your elbows bend, keeping your shoulders controlled.
description: This seated machine dip moves the handles downward while the torso remains seated, working the triceps with help from the chest and shoulders.

name: Weight-Stack Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit at the machine and rest the backs of your upper arms on the sloped pad.
Grip the handle with palms facing up and let your elbows lengthen without forcing them straight.
Curl the handle upward while keeping your upper arms on the pad.
Lower the handle slowly through the same path.
description: A weight-stack preacher curl supports the upper arms on a pad while the biceps bend the elbows.

name: Machine Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit with your chest against the front edge of the preacher pad and your upper arms resting on it.
Hold the machine bar with palms facing up.
Bend your elbows to curl the bar toward your shoulders without lifting your upper arms.
Lower the lever slowly until your elbows are nearly straight.
description: A seated machine curl bends the elbows while the upper arms rest on a sloped pad. The biceps lift the handles against the machine resistance.

name: Seated Machine Pullover
instructions: Sit with your back against the pad and your feet planted on the floor.
Reach overhead to hold the lever handles and rest your upper arms against the arm pads with your elbows bent.
Pull the lever in an arc from above your head down toward your abdomen while keeping your torso supported.
Allow the handles to travel back overhead slowly without arching your lower back.
description: A seated machine pullover moves the arms through an overhead-to-abdomen arc to work the lats.

name: Underhand Machine Pulldown
instructions: Sit with your thighs secured beneath the pads and both feet planted.
Take the overhead handles with palms facing toward you.
Draw your elbows down beside your torso to bring the handles toward your upper chest.
Return the handles overhead under control, keeping your torso steady.
description: This machine pulldown uses an underhand grip to work the lats and biceps as the handles descend in front of the body.

name: Machine Reverse-Grip Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit with your upper arms supported on the preacher pad.
Grip the handle with palms facing down and keep your wrists aligned with your forearms.
Bend your elbows to lift the handle without raising your upper arms.
Lower the lever slowly until your arms are nearly straight.
description: An overhand grip changes the feel of this machine curl. Bend the elbows to lift the handles while the upper-arm and forearm muscles work together.

name: Underhand Machine Seated Row
instructions: Sit facing the machine with your chest against the pad and feet supported.
Grasp both handles with palms facing up.
Pull the handles toward your ribs, moving your elbows back close to your sides.
Return the handles forward slowly while keeping your chest supported.
description: The underhand seated row uses supported lever resistance to train the lats, upper back and biceps.

name: Machine Reverse Hyperextension
instructions: Lie face down with your abdomen and hips on the support pad and your legs hanging below its edge.
Secure the lower legs in the machine attachment and hold the front handles with forearms supported.
Lift both legs backward through the hips until they approach the line of your torso.
Lower them slowly without swinging the load or lifting your abdomen from the pad.
description: The reverse hyperextension lifts the legs behind a supported torso to work the glutes and hamstrings.

name: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row
instructions: Stand on the machine footplates and lean your chest onto the angled pad.
Reach down and take the row handles with palms facing down.
Pull the handles toward your ribs while keeping your chest on the pad.
Lower the lever slowly until your arms lengthen, maintaining contact with the support.
description: This T-bar row supports the chest on an inclined pad while the upper back and lats pull the lever upward.

name: Seated Rotary Calf Press
instructions: Sit against the backrest with your legs nearly straight and the balls of your feet on the rotating footplate.
Hold the side handles and keep your knees at a steady slight bend.
Press the footplate away by pointing your toes through the ankles.
Let the footplate rotate back slowly as your ankles bend toward you.
description: The rotary calf press moves a rotating footplate with the ankles while the torso and thighs stay supported.

name: Reclined Machine Calf Press
instructions: Sit against the reclined back pad and place the balls of your feet on the lower part of the footplate, leaving your heels free.
Adjust your position so your legs are nearly straight, then hold the side handles.
Push through the balls of your feet to move the plate away, keeping the knee angle steady.
Return slowly by letting your ankles bend toward your body.
description: This reclined calf press trains the calves by moving the footplate through the ankles rather than pressing it with repeated knee bends.

name: Plate-Loaded Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Sit with the balls of your feet on the raised foot support and your heels hanging free.
Position the thigh pad over your legs just above the knees and hold the handles.
Raise your heels to lift the padded lever, keeping your knees bent.
Lower your heels slowly below the support level through a comfortable range.
description: The seated calf raise loads the thighs while bent knees and rising heels emphasize the soleus within the calf muscles.

name: Seated Machine Crunch with Upper-Arm Pads
instructions: Sit upright with your feet on the supports and take the handles beside your head.
Keep the moving pads in firm contact with your upper body as you hold the handles.
Gently tighten your abdomen and curl your chest toward your pelvis without pulling with your arms.
Return slowly to the upright starting position without reclining far backward.
description: This seated machine crunch bends the torso forward against lever resistance to work the abs.

name: Seated Machine Crunch with Chest Pad
instructions: Sit facing the moving pad with your chest against it and both feet supported.
Rest your forearms or hands on the pad handles to keep contact.
Tighten your abdomen and curl forward, bringing your ribs toward your pelvis as you press the pad down.
Return upright slowly without pushing the movement through your arms.
description: The chest-pad machine crunch flexes the torso forward against a pad to work the abdominal muscles.

name: Seated Overhead-Handle Machine Crunch
instructions: Sit with your hips in the seat and feet on the machine supports.
Reach up to hold the handles beside your head and keep your elbows bent.
Curl your upper body toward your thighs by drawing your ribs toward your pelvis.
Let the lever return slowly until you are upright, keeping your hips on the seat.
description: This machine crunch uses overhead handles while the abs curl the torso forward from a supported seated position.

name: Upright Seated Machine Dip
instructions: Sit upright on the machine with both feet flat on the floor.
Hold the handles beside your hips and begin with your elbows bent.
Press the handles downward until your arms are nearly straight, keeping your body seated.
Let the handles rise slowly while your elbows bend back to the starting position.
description: The upright seated machine dip trains the triceps by pressing lever handles downward without lowering the body from the seat.

name: Seated Machine Chest Fly
instructions: Sit with your back against the pad and adjust the handles to about chest height.
Hold the handles with a small bend in your elbows and open your arms to a comfortable width.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest while keeping that elbow bend.
Open the arms slowly to return without lifting your back from the pad.
description: The seated machine fly brings the arms together across the chest to work the pectoral muscles.

name: Seated Cable Good Morning
instructions: Sit on the cable station with both feet braced on its footplates and knees slightly bent.
Hold the low cable bar with both hands and keep your arms long.
Lean forward from your hips while keeping your back steady.
Keep your hips on the seat and raise your torso to upright without bending your elbows or leaning far back.
Return slowly to the forward lean, keeping the cable under tension.
description: Leaning forward and back from the hips against a low cable works the lower back and hip muscles while the arms hold the handle steady.

name: Seated Machine Hip Abduction
instructions: Sit against the backrest with your feet on the supports and the pads against the outsides of your thighs.
Hold the side handles and keep your hips in the seat.
Push your knees apart against the pads without rocking your torso.
Bring the legs together slowly until you reach the starting position.
description: Seated machine hip abduction moves the thighs apart against resistance to work the muscles along the outer hips.

name: Seated Machine Hip Adduction
instructions: Sit against the backrest with the pads against the insides of your thighs and your feet on the supports.
Set a comfortable starting width and hold the side handles.
Bring your knees toward each other by pressing inward against the pads.
Open the legs slowly to the starting width without letting the weight drop.
description: The seated hip-adduction machine works the inner-thigh muscles by bringing the thighs together.

name: Seated Machine Leg Curl
instructions: Sit against the backrest with the moving roller behind your lower legs just above the heels.
Secure the upper pad across your thighs and hold the handles.
Bend your knees to pull your heels downward and back beneath the seat, keeping your thighs still.
Let your legs straighten slowly as the roller returns forward.
description: The seated leg curl pulls the heels down and back against a roller to work the hamstrings.

name: Machine Crunch with Knee Raise
instructions: Sit in the machine with your back supported, feet in the lower supports and hands on the overhead handles.
Gently tighten your abdomen while keeping your hips in the seat.
Curl your torso forward and draw your knees upward together, bringing your ribs and pelvis closer.
Return both the upper and lower levers slowly without dropping your legs or arching your back.
description: This machine combines a forward crunch and knee raise, working the abs while the hip flexors lift the thighs.

name: Overhand Machine Reverse Fly
instructions: Sit facing the machine with your chest against the pad and feet planted.
Grasp the handles with palms facing down and keep a small bend in your elbows.
Open both arms out to the sides and back while keeping your chest on the pad.
Bring the handles forward slowly without changing the elbow bend.
description: The overhand machine reverse fly moves the arms apart to work the rear deltoids and upper back.

name: Neutral-Grip Machine Reverse Fly
instructions: Sit facing the chest pad with both feet on the floor.
Hold the upright handles with palms facing each other and elbows slightly bent.
Draw your arms outward and backward, keeping your torso against the pad.
Return the handles forward slowly while maintaining the same elbow bend.
description: This reverse fly uses a neutral grip while the rear deltoids and upper back open the arms against machine resistance.

name: Overhand Machine Seated Row
instructions: Sit with your chest against the support pad and feet on the machine supports.
Hold the handles with palms facing down and your arms extended forward.
Pull the handles toward your ribs as your elbows move behind you.
Return slowly, allowing your arms to lengthen while your chest stays on the pad.
description: This supported machine row uses an overhand grip to work the upper back, lats and elbow flexors.

name: Seated Leg Press with Calf Press
instructions: Sit against the leg-press backrest with the balls of both feet securely on the lower footplate and your heels free.
Hold the side handles and extend your knees and hips to press the seat away from the plate.
With your knees nearly straight, push through the balls of your feet to extend your ankles.
Let your ankles bend back under control, then bend your knees and hips to return to the start.
Repeat the leg-press and calf-press phases as one sequence without forcefully locking your knees.
description: This combination joins a seated leg press with an ankle press, working the quadriceps, glutes and calves through distinct phases.
aliases: Lever Seated Squat Calf Raise on Leg Press Machine

name: Angled Lever Squat to Press
instructions: Stand facing the pivoted lever with feet about shoulder-width apart and hold both handles near your shoulders.
Keep the load close as you bend your hips and knees into a controlled squat.
Push through your feet to stand, then continue by pressing the handles upward and forward until your arms are long.
Lower the handles back to your shoulders under control.
Begin the next squat with the handles close to your body.
description: The angled lever squat to press combines a squat with a two-arm press, working the quadriceps and glutes before the shoulders and triceps complete the lift.

name: Plate-Loaded Wide-Grip Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit with your back against the pad and feet on the floor.
Take the wide handles with palms facing forward and elbows below your hands.
Press the handles upward until your arms are long, keeping your torso supported.
Lower them slowly to the starting height.
description: The wide-grip shoulder press raises two plate-loaded levers overhead to work the shoulders and triceps.

name: Seated Shoulder Press with Foot Supports
instructions: Sit against the machine backrest with both feet on its supports.
Hold the handles beside your shoulders and keep your elbows beneath your hands.
Press both handles upward along the lever path without lifting your back from the pad.
Return the handles slowly to shoulder height.
description: This seated shoulder press supports the feet and torso while the shoulders and triceps lift the machine levers overhead.

name: Standing Lever Shrug
instructions: Stand between the lever handles with feet planted and arms by your sides.
Grip the handles and stand tall, keeping your elbows straight but relaxed.
Raise both shoulders toward your ears without bending your arms or knees.
Lower your shoulders slowly back to the starting position.
description: The standing lever shrug raises handles beside the body through shoulder elevation, working the upper trapezius.

name: Standing Machine Calf Raise
instructions: Place the balls of your feet on the raised platform with your heels free to move.
Position your shoulders beneath the pads, hold the handles and stand with your knees nearly straight.
Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet.
Lower your heels slowly through a comfortable range while keeping your torso upright.
description: The standing machine calf raise adds shoulder-pad resistance as the calf muscles lift the heels.

name: Standing Machine Chest Press
instructions: Stand on the machine platform with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles at chest height and gently tighten your abdomen.
Press the handles forward until your arms are nearly straight.
Keep your back against the pad as you slowly bend your elbows and return the handles toward your chest.
description: A standing chest press uses a supported lever machine to train the chest, triceps and shoulders.

name: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row
instructions: Stand on the footplates and lean your chest onto the machine pad.
Grip the handles with your palms facing down and let your arms lengthen.
Pull the handles toward your ribs, drawing your elbows back.
Lower the lever slowly without lifting your chest from the pad.
description: A standing, chest-supported row trains the upper back and lats using a loaded T-bar lever.

name: Underhand T-Bar Row on Footplates
instructions: Stand on the machine's footplates and bend at your hips and knees to reach the handles.
Take the handles with palms facing upward and let your arms extend.
Keep your torso steady and pull your elbows back to bring the handles toward your lower ribs.
Lower the handles slowly until your arms are long, maintaining the same forward lean.
description: An underhand T-bar row works the back and elbow flexors while the legs hold a bent-over stance on the machine's footplates.

name: Seated Machine Triceps Extension
instructions: Sit facing the machine arm pad and rest your upper arms on it.
Hold the handles with your elbows bent and aligned with the machine pivot.
Straighten your elbows to move the handles down and forward.
Bend your elbows slowly to return while keeping your upper arms on the pad.
description: This supported triceps extension moves the handles by straightening the elbows, with the upper arms resting on a front pad.

name: Supported Single-Arm Cable Row
instructions: Place one knee and the forearm on the same side on the station pads, with your other foot on the floor.
Grip the low cable handle with your free hand and keep your back steady.
Pull the handle toward your waist by moving your elbow behind you.
Let the working arm straighten slowly without twisting your torso.
Repeat on the other side.
description: A single-arm low cable row uses knee and forearm supports while the free arm pulls toward the waist.

name: Rope Climb with Feet Supported
instructions: Secure a climbing rope to a suitable overhead anchor and face it.
Grip the rope with both hands and brace your feet on the low frame rail, keeping your knees bent.
Lean back and move your hands down the rope one at a time to lower your body.
Pull hand over hand to raise yourself back toward the anchor while keeping your feet braced.
Use a controlled range and maintain your grip throughout.
description: A supported rope climb raises and lowers the body with alternating hand pulls while the feet stay braced on a low rail.

name: Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, about hip-width apart.
Place your arms beside you and gently tighten your abdomen.
Press through your feet and lift your hips until your trunk and thighs form a line.
Lower your hips to the floor with control, keeping your knees aligned with your feet.
description: A floor bridge trains the glutes by lifting the pelvis while the upper back and feet stay on the floor.

name: Prone Back Extension
instructions: Lie face down with your legs long and arms by your sides.
Keep your feet on the floor and your neck in line with your spine.
Raise your chest a short distance using your back muscles, without throwing your head backward.
Lower your chest slowly to the floor.
description: A small, controlled upper-body lift from a face-down position works the spinal extensor muscles.

name: Alternating Reverse Lunge to Knee-Drive Jump
instructions: Stand tall, then step one foot backward and lower into a lunge.
Push through the front foot and drive the rear knee forward and up as you jump.
Land softly on the supporting foot and bring the other foot down to regain a stable standing position.
Step the other leg back and repeat the lunge and knee-drive jump.
Reset your balance between sides.
description: This sequence combines a reverse lunge with a single-leg jump and knee drive, resetting upright before changing sides.

name: Forward Lunge with Rotation
instructions: Stand tall with your elbows bent and hands in front of your chest.
Step forward and bend both knees into a lunge.
Rotate your upper body toward the front leg while keeping the knee aligned with the foot.
Turn back to face forward and push off the front foot to stand.
Finish your repetitions, then change the lead leg.
description: A forward lunge and trunk turn combine leg strength with controlled rotation.

name: Side-Lying Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Lie on your side with your hips stacked and your lower arm supporting your head.
Bend your top knee and hold that ankle with your top hand.
Draw your heel gently toward your buttock while keeping your pelvis steady and thighs close together.
Hold a comfortable stretch, release slowly, then change sides.
description: A side-lying heel-to-buttock stretch lengthens the front of the thigh.

name: Figure-Four Cross-Body Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with one foot flat and the other ankle resting across that thigh.
Place your hands lightly behind your head without pulling on your neck.
Curl and rotate your upper body to bring the opposite shoulder toward the raised knee.
Lower your shoulders with control while keeping your legs in position.
Finish the repetitions and switch the crossed leg.
description: A cross-body crunch with one ankle resting over the opposite thigh trains the abdominal muscles and obliques.

name: Flat Bench Straight-Leg Raise
instructions: Lie on your back on a flat bench with your legs extending beyond the end.
Hold the bench beside your hips and gently tighten your abdomen.
Raise both legs together toward vertical, keeping them nearly straight.
Lower them slowly toward bench height without arching your lower back.
description: Straight-leg raises on a bench move at the hips while the abdominal muscles stabilize the pelvis.

name: Flat Bench Leg Raise with Hip Curl
instructions: Lie on your back along a flat bench and hold its sides near your head.
Extend your legs beyond the bench and gently tighten your abdomen.
Raise your legs, then curl your pelvis upward to lift your hips slightly from the bench.
Set your hips down first, then lower your legs with control.
Keep the movement smooth rather than swinging your legs.
description: This bench exercise combines a leg raise with a small reverse crunch that lifts the pelvis.

name: Close-Grip Seated Machine Chest Press
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are level with your chest and sit against the back pad.
Hold the close handles with your elbows bent beside your torso.
Press forward until your arms are nearly straight.
Return the handles slowly without lifting your back from the pad.
description: A seated close-grip chest press works the chest and triceps through the machine lever path.

name: Wall Sit March
instructions: Place your back against a wall and walk your feet forward.
Slide down into a wall sit with your knees bent and feet flat.
Keep your back against the wall as you lift one knee and foot slightly.
Set that foot down and lift the other, keeping your hips at a steady height.
Stand up to finish.
description: A wall sit with alternating knee lifts loads the supporting leg while the trunk stays braced against the wall.

name: Medicine Ball Overhead Downward Throw
instructions: Stand with your feet apart and hold a medicine ball in both hands.
Raise the ball in front of you, then bend your elbows to bring it behind your head.
Gently tighten your abdomen and drive the ball forward and down in front of you.
Lean forward from your hips as you follow through, then regain control of the ball low in front of your legs.
Stand and reset before the next throw.
description: This medicine ball throw loads the ball behind the head before a forward and downward arm drive, followed by a low recovery.
aliases: Medicine Ball Catch and Overhead Throw

name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
instructions: Stand facing your partner in a staggered stance and hold the medicine ball at your chest.
Gently tighten your abdomen and shift your weight toward the front foot.
Extend both arms quickly to pass the ball forward to your partner.
Receive the return with bent elbows, bring the ball back to your chest and reset your stance.
description: A two-handed chest pass sends the ball to a partner, who returns it. The chest and triceps produce the forward push with a small transfer of bodyweight.

name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass from Three-Point Stance
instructions: Place the medicine ball on the floor and crouch with one hand resting on it.
Stand as you lift the ball, bringing both hands onto it and raising it to your chest.
Dip slightly through your knees and hips, then extend your legs and arms to throw the ball forward.
Regain your balance and retrieve the ball.
Reset in the three-point stance before repeating.
description: Start in a crouch with one hand on a medicine ball, then stand and lift it to your chest. A quick dip and extension of the legs and arms drives the ball forward in a chest pass.
aliases: Medicine Ball Chest Push from 3 Point Stance

name: Kneeling Medicine Ball Chest Pass with Push-Up Return
instructions: Kneel upright and hold the medicine ball at your chest.
Throw the ball forward forcefully and allow your body to tip forward from your knees.
Place both hands on the floor and bend your elbows to absorb the landing.
Push off the floor to return your torso to upright kneeling.
Recover the ball and reset for another repetition.
description: A kneeling chest throw flows into a forward landing on the hands and an explosive push back to kneeling.
aliases: Medicine Ball Chest Push Multiple Response

name: Kneeling Medicine Ball Chest Pass with Forward Fall
instructions: Kneel upright with a medicine ball held at your chest.
Extend your arms to throw the ball forward while allowing your body to lean forward from the knees.
Catch your body with your hands on the floor and bend your elbows to lower under control.
Gently tighten your abdomen as you absorb the landing.
Return to kneeling and recover the ball before the next repetition.
description: This kneeling chest pass finishes with a controlled forward fall and landing on the hands.
aliases: Medicine Ball Chest Push Single Response

name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass with Leg Drive
instructions: Stand with your feet planted, hips and knees bent, and a medicine ball held near your waist.
Straighten your legs and torso while bringing the ball to your chest.
Extend both arms to throw the ball forward into a clear area, keeping your feet planted.
Retrieve the ball and reset your stance before repeating.
description: Extend the legs and torso, bring a medicine ball to the chest, and throw it forward with both arms while keeping the feet planted.
aliases: Medicine Ball Chest Push with Run Release
Medicine Ball Chest Pass with Run-Through

name: Close-Grip Medicine Ball Push-Up
instructions: Place a stable medicine ball on the floor and set both hands close together on top.
Step your feet back into a straight-body plank.
Bend your elbows beside your torso to lower your chest toward the ball.
Press through your hands to straighten your arms without letting the ball roll or your hips sag.
description: A close-hand push-up on a medicine ball works the triceps and chest while challenging upper-body stability.
aliases: Medicine Ball Close Grip Push Up

name: Medicine Ball Overhead Slam
instructions: Stand with your feet apart and raise a medicine ball overhead.
Gently tighten your abdomen and drive the ball down toward the floor in front of you.
Bend through your hips and knees as you follow the throw, keeping your balance.
Regain control of the ball after it lands and stand to reset.
description: An overhead slam combines a downward arm drive with trunk and leg movement to accelerate a medicine ball into the floor.

name: Supine Medicine Ball Chest Throw
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a medicine ball above your chest and bend your elbows to bring it toward you.
Press quickly to toss the ball a short distance straight upward.
Catch it with both hands and bend your elbows to absorb the return before repeating.
description: A lying chest throw develops an explosive chest and triceps press from the floor.

name: Mixed-Grip Pull-Up
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar with one palm facing you and the other facing away.
Hang with your arms extended and gently tighten your abdomen.
Pull until your chin clears the bar without kicking.
Lower under control to the hang.
Reverse your hand positions for the next set.
description: A pull-up with one overhand and one underhand grip trains the back and elbow flexors.

name: Modified Hindu Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a high plank with your hands and toes on the floor and your body in a straight line.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest close to the floor.
Press through your hands as you straighten your arms and send your hips up and back into an inverted V.
Shift your body forward with your arms straight until you return to the high plank.
Lower your chest again and repeat the sequence with control.
description: A modified Hindu push-up combines a low push-up position, an inverted V and a straight-arm plank. The chest, shoulders and triceps move the body between these positions.

name: Kneeling Bodyweight Triceps Extension
instructions: Kneel with your palms on the floor ahead of your shoulders.
Gently tighten your abdomen and bend both elbows to lower your forearms to the floor.
Keep your knees planted and elbows pointing forward.
Press through your palms to lift your forearms and straighten your elbows.
description: A knees-supported bodyweight triceps extension lowers the forearms and presses back onto the hands.
aliases: Modified Push Up to Lower Arms

name: Bodyweight Monster Walk
instructions: Stand with feet apart and knees softly bent, with your hands on your hips.
Take a controlled diagonal step forward and outward.
Step the other foot forward and outward, maintaining a wide stance.
Continue alternating steps without letting your knees collapse inward.
description: A wide, diagonal walking drill moves one leg at a time without a resistance band.

name: Mountain Climber
instructions: Set your hands beneath your shoulders in a high plank.
Bring one knee toward your chest while the other leg stays extended.
Switch legs in a controlled running action.
Keep your hips steady and breathe continuously as you alternate.
description: Alternating knee drives from a high plank combine conditioning with trunk and shoulder support.

name: Ring Pull-Up
instructions: Hang from securely anchored gymnastic rings with your arms long.
Gently tighten your abdomen and pull your elbows down toward your ribs.
Raise your body until the rings are near your upper chest, allowing them to rotate naturally.
Lower slowly back to the hang without swinging.
description: A ring pull-up raises the chest toward freely rotating rings and trains the lats and elbow flexors.

name: Bar Muscle-Up
instructions: Hang from a fixed horizontal bar with your palms facing away from you.
Use a coordinated pull and controlled body swing to bring your chest high toward the bar.
Move your shoulders and wrists over the bar as your elbows turn behind you.
Press down on the bar to straighten your arms above it.
Bend your arms and lower through the transition to a controlled hang.
description: A bar muscle-up combines a high pull, turnover and press into straight-arm support above the bar.

name: Close-Grip Push-Up with Feet on Stability Ball
instructions: Place your lower shins and feet on a stability ball and your hands close together on the floor.
Gently tighten your abdomen to keep your body aligned.
Bend your elbows beside your torso and lower your chest toward the floor.
Press back up without letting the ball roll away.
description: A close-grip push-up with the feet elevated on a stability ball trains the triceps and chest.

name: Standing Neck Side Stretch
instructions: Stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and hands behind your back.
Slowly tilt your head to one side, bringing your ear toward your shoulder without raising that shoulder.
Hold a gentle stretch, then return your head to the center.
Repeat to the other side without forcing the range.
description: A gentle sideways head tilt stretches the muscles along the side of the neck.

name: Bench Crunch with Controlled Lowering
instructions: Lie on the abdominal bench with your feet secured beneath its rollers.
Rest your hands lightly behind your head and gently tighten your abdomen.
Curl your shoulders and upper back away from the bench.
Lower slowly until your back returns to the pad, keeping your neck relaxed.
description: A foot-secured bench crunch emphasizes a controlled lowering phase.

name: Bench-Supported Oblique Crunch
instructions: Lie on the floor with your lower legs resting on a bench and knees bent.
Place one hand lightly behind your head and rest the other arm beside you on the floor.
Curl the shoulder of the raised arm toward the opposite knee with a small torso turn.
Lower slowly and finish the repetitions before changing sides.
description: An oblique crunch turns the chest toward the opposite knee while both lower legs rest on a bench.

name: Side-Lying Oblique Crunch
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs extended and stacked.
Place your top hand lightly behind your head and use the lower arm for support.
Lift your shoulder and upper torso sideways toward your hip without pulling on your neck.
Lower slowly and finish the repetitions before changing sides.
description: A side-lying crunch lifts the upper torso sideways to work the obliques.

name: Neutral-Grip Bar Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand tall holding the parallel handles of a neutral-grip curl bar, palms facing each other.
Keep your upper arms close to your sides.
Bend your elbows to curl the bar toward your chest.
Lower it slowly to straight arms without swinging your torso.
description: A specialty bar keeps both hands neutral during the curl, training the elbow flexors.

name: Seated Neutral-Grip Bar Overhead Triceps Extension
instructions: Sit on a flat bench with both feet planted.
Hold the parallel handles of a neutral-grip bar and raise it above your head.
Keep your upper arms near your head as you bend your elbows to lower the bar behind it.
Straighten your elbows to raise the bar overhead while keeping your trunk steady.
description: A seated overhead extension uses a neutral-grip specialty bar to train the triceps.

name: Single-Arm Wall Lat Stretch
instructions: Stand beside a wall with the near arm raised overhead.
Bend that elbow and place it against the wall above head height.
Let your torso move gently away from the supported arm until you feel a stretch along your side.
Hold comfortably, release and change sides.
description: An overhead arm supported against a wall creates a stretch along the lats and back of the upper arm.

name: Frame-Assisted Single-Arm Chin-Up
instructions: Grip the overhead bar with one hand with your palm facing you.
Hold the frame upright with your other hand for assistance and lift your feet from the floor.
Pull with the overhead arm, using the frame hand only as much as needed to raise your chin above the bar.
Lower slowly, keeping both grips secure.
Repeat with the opposite overhead hand.
description: A chin-up emphasizes one overhead arm while the other hand helps by holding the frame upright.

name: Single-Arm Bench Dip with Leg Raised
instructions: Sit at the bench edge and place one hand beside your hip.
Plant one foot on the floor and extend the other leg forward off the floor, with your free arm reaching forward.
Shift your hips off the edge and bend the supporting elbow to lower a comfortable distance.
Press through the bench hand and planted foot to rise.
Finish the repetitions and switch arms.
description: A bench dip uses one arm and one planted foot while the other leg stays raised.

name: Single-Arm Medicine Ball Slam
instructions: Stand with feet apart and hold a manageable medicine ball in one hand.
Raise that arm overhead while gently tightening your abdomen.
Drive the ball down to the floor, bending your hips and knees with the throw.
Recover the ball under control and reset.
Repeat with the other arm.
description: A one-handed overhead slam combines the throwing arm with trunk and leg movement.

name: Single-Arm Anchored Towel Row
instructions: Secure a strong towel to a fixed support at about chest height.
Hold it with one hand, bend your knees and lean back while keeping your feet planted.
Pull your torso toward the anchor by drawing the working elbow back.
Extend the arm slowly to lean away again without twisting your torso.
Repeat with the other arm.
description: An anchored towel provides a grip for a single-arm bodyweight row performed while leaning backward.

name: Single-Leg Donkey Calf Raise
instructions: Push your hips back, lean forward from your hips and place both hands on a stable bench.
Keep one foot on the floor and bend the other knee to lift that foot.
Raise the working heel, keeping its knee nearly straight.
Lower the heel to the floor with control.
Change legs after the set.
description: A single-leg calf raise is performed while leaning forward with both hands on a bench.

name: Single-Leg Floor Calf Raise
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other foot lifted.
Keep your trunk upright and the working knee nearly straight.
Rise onto the ball of the standing foot.
Lower your heel slowly to the floor.
Repeat with the other leg.
description: A single-leg heel raise from the floor trains the calf while requiring balance.

name: Bodyweight Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
instructions: Stand in front of a stable low box and rest the top of one foot behind you on it.
Keep the front foot far enough forward to lower comfortably.
Bend the front knee and hip, lowering the rear knee toward the floor.
Drive through the front foot to stand while the rear foot stays supported.
Repeat with the other leg in front.
description: A split squat with the rear foot elevated trains the front leg without external weight.

name: Otis Sit-Up
