description: The left side of the head presses against a loaded machine pad. The neck bends sideways while the torso and shoulders remain still.
aliases: Lever Neck Left Side Flexion (Plate Loaded)

name: Plate-Loaded Machine Right Neck Side Bend
instructions: Set the seat and pad so the right side of your head rests against the head pad above the ear.
Sit upright with your feet planted and hands holding the machine handles.
Tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder to move the loaded pad.
Keep your shoulders level and avoid rotating your head.
Return under control through the same comfortable range.
description: A machine pad resists side bending toward the right. The neck muscles move the head while the supported torso remains steady.
aliases: Lever Neck Right Side Flexion (Plate Loaded)

name: Rear-Leg Hook Kick
instructions: Start in a staggered fighting stance with your hands raised.
Shift onto the front leg and turn the supporting foot as you lift the rear knee.
Extend the kicking leg outward, then sweep the heel across the front of your body in a hooking arc.
Bend the kicking knee again and place that foot back in its rear starting position.
Regain your balance before repeating, then change stance to train the other leg.
description: The rear leg extends and sweeps across in a hook before returning to its original stance. The glutes and hip muscles guide the arc while the hamstrings bend the knee.

name: Front-Leg Hook Kick
instructions: Stand in a fighting stance with your hands up and weight ready to shift onto the rear leg.
Lift the front knee while turning the supporting foot to allow the hips to open.
Extend the front leg slightly past the intended line of the kick.
Sweep the heel inward across that line, then bend the knee to bring the foot back.
Set the front foot down under control and repeat before changing stance.
description: The lead leg makes an inward hooking sweep while the rear leg supports the body. The hip adductors and glutes guide the leg and the hamstrings assist the hook.

name: Low Front Kick
instructions: Stand in a staggered stance with your hands raised and weight balanced.
Shift onto the support leg and lift the kicking knee in front of your body.
Extend the lower leg forward into a low kick, with the foot extended in the direction of the kick.
Bend the knee to bring the foot back without locking the joint at full extension.
Return the foot to your stance and reset before repeating or changing legs.
description: A forward knee lift leads into a low snapping kick. The hip flexors raise the thigh and the quadriceps extend the knee.

name: Rear-Leg Axe Kick
instructions: Begin in a staggered fighting stance with your hands raised.
Shift onto the front leg and lift the rear leg upward in front of your body.
Extend the kicking leg toward your available high range with the heel leading.
Bring the heel downward in a controlled arc while keeping the supporting knee soft.
Return the foot to the rear stance and regain balance before repeating.
description: The rear leg rises high and then sweeps downward in an axe-like path. The hip flexors lift the leg while the hamstrings and glutes control its downward return.

name: Front Snap Kick
instructions: Take a staggered fighting stance with both hands raised.
Shift onto the support leg and lift the kicking knee in front of your hips.
Extend the lower leg forward quickly while keeping the toes drawn back from the ball of the foot.
Bend the knee to bring the foot back immediately without locking the joint.
Place the foot back in your stance, then repeat or change legs.
description: A knee lift is followed by a quick straightening and bending of the lower leg. The quadriceps straighten the knee while the hip flexors hold the thigh up.

name: Spinning Hook Kick
instructions: Begin in a fighting stance with your hands raised.
Turn on the supporting foot and look around first to find the direction of the kick.
Continue the hip turn as you lift and extend the kicking leg.
Sweep the heel across in a hooking arc, then bend the knee to bring the leg back.
Finish the turn and place the foot down in a balanced stance.
Reset fully before repeating or changing sides.
description: A turn of the body leads into a high hooking sweep of one leg. The hips, trunk and supporting leg coordinate the spin and recovery.

name: Side Kick
instructions: Stand in a fighting stance with your hands raised.
Shift onto one leg and turn that foot away from the direction of the kick.
Lift the other knee toward your torso, then drive its heel outward to the side.
Keep the supporting knee soft and control the torso angle as the leg extends.
Bend the kicking knee again and place the foot down.
Reset your balance before repeating on either side.
description: The kicking leg extends sideways from a bent-knee position while the support foot pivots. The glutes guide the hip and the quadriceps straighten the knee.

name: Roundhouse Kick
instructions: Stand in a staggered fighting stance with your hands raised.
Turn the supporting foot as you lift the kicking knee and rotate your hips.
Extend the lower leg in a horizontal arc across the front of your body.
Keep your balance as you bend the knee to bring the foot back.
Place the foot back down under control and reset before repeating.
description: The hips turn as one leg delivers an arcing kick. The quadriceps extend the knee while the glutes and trunk help direct the movement.

name: Heel Push Kick
instructions: Start in a staggered stance with your hands raised.
Shift onto the support leg and lift the kicking knee toward your chest.
Draw the toes back and extend the leg forward, leading with the heel in a pushing action.
Bend the knee to bring the foot back toward your body.
Set the foot down in your starting stance and repeat with control.
description: The heel drives forward from a high knee position before the leg bends back toward the body. The quadriceps and hip flexors control the kick while the other leg provides balance.

name: Spinning Back Kick
instructions: Start in a fighting stance with your hands raised.
Turn on the front foot and look over your shoulder toward the direction of the kick.
Lift the rear knee as the hips turn, then drive that heel straight backward.
Incline your torso as needed for balance while keeping the supporting knee soft.
Bend the kicking knee to bring the leg back and place it down in your stance.
Reset before the next repetition.
description: A body turn leads into a straight backward kick with the rear heel. The glutes extend the hip and the quadriceps straighten the knee.

name: Incline Prone Neck Extension with Head Harness
instructions: Secure the weighted head harness and lie face down along an incline bench with your head beyond its upper edge.
Plant your feet and keep your chest supported while the plate hangs freely.
Lower your head gently through a comfortable range.
Extend your neck to bring your head back into line with your torso.
Lower slowly without lifting your chest or swinging the plate.
description: An incline bench supports the chest while a weighted harness resists neck extension. The head moves independently of the supported torso.
aliases: Weighted Lying Neck Extension (With Head Harness)

name: Incline Neck Flexion with Head Harness
instructions: Fasten the weighted head harness and lie face up on an incline bench with your head free of the upper edge.
Keep your back supported and feet planted as the plate hangs beneath your head.
Nod your chin toward your chest and lift your head through a comfortable range.
Keep the shoulders on the bench and avoid pulling with the torso.
Lower your head slowly to the starting position.
description: The back rests on an incline bench while the neck curls forward against a harness load. The torso remains supported throughout.
aliases: Weighted Lying Neck Flexion (With Head Harness)

name: Standing Neck Extension with Head Harness
instructions: Secure the weighted harness and stand with your feet apart and knees softly bent.
Lean forward slightly at the hips and rest your hands on your thighs to steady your torso while the plate hangs freely.
Lower your chin gently without rounding your upper back.
Extend your neck to raise your head into line with your torso.
Return slowly without swinging the weight.
description: A slight forward lean allows the harness weight to hang below the head. The neck extends and lowers while the legs and torso stay still.
aliases: Weighted Standing Neck Extension (With Head Harness)

name: Seated Low-Cable Neck Extension
instructions: Connect a head harness to a low cable and sit facing the machine on a stable upright bench.
Secure the harness and sit far enough away for light cable tension with your feet planted.
Begin with the head gently lowered while keeping your torso still.
Extend your neck to raise your head into a comfortable upright position.
Return slowly, resisting the cable without arching your back.
description: A low cable in front of the body resists neck extension through a head harness. The seated torso stays upright as the head moves.
aliases: Cable Seated Neck Extension (With Head Harness)

name: Seated Cable Neck Flexion
instructions: Set the cable near seated head height and attach it to the back of a head harness.
Sit facing away from the machine with your feet planted and back supported.
Keep your shoulders still as you nod and lower your chin toward your chest.
Move only through a comfortable neck range without rounding your torso.
Return slowly to the starting head position against the cable tension.
description: A cable behind the head resists a forward neck curl. The seat and backrest support the torso during the movement.
aliases: Cable Seated Neck Flexion (With Head Harness)

name: Backward Rollover to Straddle Forward Reach
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in a wide straddle.
Roll backward under control, bringing your legs overhead while supporting the movement across your upper back and shoulders.
Reverse the roll and return your hips to the floor.
Open your legs into the wide straddle and reach your arms and torso forward between them.
Rise slightly from the reach and repeat the smooth rollover sequence.
description: A backward rollover flows into a wide seated straddle reach with the legs on the floor. The abs control the rolling action and the forward reach stretches the inner and back thighs.

name: Standing Toe Raise
instructions: Stand upright with your feet about hip-width apart.
Keep both heels on the floor and shift your balance slightly toward them.
Lift your forefeet and toes toward your shins without bending your torso.
Lower the fronts of your feet slowly and repeat.
description: The forefeet rise while the heels remain grounded. The tibialis anterior at the front of the shins produces ankle dorsiflexion.

name: Dumbbell Rear-Foot-Elevated Step and Split Squat
instructions: Place two stable benches a stride apart and stand between them holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Rest the toes of your rear foot on the bench behind you while the front foot starts on the floor.
Lift the front foot onto the bench in front of you.
With both feet now elevated, bend the front knee and lower into a controlled split squat.
Rise from the squat and return the front foot to the floor while keeping the rear foot supported.
Complete the set, then switch legs.
description: The front foot steps from the floor onto a bench before a split squat between two benches. The rear foot remains elevated throughout the sequence.

name: Barbell Step Jump to Reverse Lunge
instructions: Hold a barbell securely across your upper back and stand facing a low stable step.
Bend your knees and hips into a squat, then jump onto the step with both feet.
Land with control and establish your balance.
Step one foot back onto the floor, then move the other foot off the step into a reverse lunge behind it.
Bend both knees to lower the lunge, then return to standing on the floor.
Reset in front of the step before repeating, changing the lunge leg between repetitions or sets.
description: A loaded jump onto a step is followed by stepping off and lowering into a reverse lunge on the floor. The quadriceps and glutes drive the jump and lunge while the bar stays on the upper back.
aliases: Barbell Squat Jump Step Rear Lunge

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat with Lower-Leg Support
instructions: Stand in the squat support with your ankles under the front rollers and calves against the rear pad.
Hold one dumbbell vertically at your chest with both hands.
Keep your lower legs supported as you bend your knees and sit your hips back.
Lower to a depth you can control while keeping the dumbbell close and torso steady.
Extend your knees and hips to return to standing.
description: A fixed lower-leg support steadies the body during a goblet squat. The dumbbell adds resistance as the quadriceps and glutes raise and lower the body.

name: Dumbbell Rear-Foot-Supported Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand on the working leg with the other toes resting lightly on a low step behind you.
Hold one dumbbell beside the front leg, place your free hand behind your back and keep a slight bend in the front knee.
Push your hips backward to lower your torso and the dumbbell beside the front leg.
Keep your back steady and most of your weight on the front foot.
Extend the front hip to return to standing, then repeat before switching legs.
description: The rear toes rest on a step while one dumbbell adds resistance as the torso leans forward over the front leg. The front-leg hamstrings and glutes control the movement.
aliases: Dumbbell Single Leg Deadlift with Stepbox Support

name: Dumbbell Sumo Pull-Through
instructions: Take a wide stance with your toes turned slightly outward and hold one dumbbell in both hands between your thighs.
Bend your knees and send your hips backward, allowing the dumbbell to travel between your legs.
Keep your back steady and your arms long as you lower.
Extend your hips and knees to stand, bringing the dumbbell forward with your body.
Lower into the next repetition without lifting the weight with your arms.
description: A wide-stance squat and hip hinge lets the dumbbell travel between the legs. The glutes and quadriceps extend the hips and knees to return upright.

name: Barbell Straddle Split Squat
instructions: Take a long split stance with the barbell passing between your legs and hold it in both hands with arms extended.
Keep the front foot flat, rear heel lifted and torso upright.
Bend both knees to lower your hips straight down while keeping the bar level beneath you.
Stop before the rear knee touches the floor, then push through your feet to rise.
Complete the set and change the lead leg.
description: The barbell is held low between the legs during a stationary split squat. The front-leg quadriceps and glutes control most of the lifting.

name: Barbell Floor Press with Raised-Leg Twists
instructions: Lie on your back holding a barbell above your chest with both arms extended.
Lift both legs off the floor and keep them together, allowing the knees to bend as you turn the legs to one side.
Sweep the raised legs across to the other side, extending the knees as they move, while holding the bar steady above your chest.
Bring the legs back toward the center and hold them elevated.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your chest, then press it back up.
Keep the legs raised and repeat the twist-and-press sequence without arching your back.
description: Raised-leg twists are followed by a barbell floor press while the legs remain elevated. The obliques and abs control the trunk while the chest and triceps perform the press.

name: Seated Band Foot Outward Rotation
instructions: Sit on a stable seat with both heels on the floor and a loop band around the fronts of your feet.
Keep one foot still to anchor the band.
Turn the other forefoot outward against the band while keeping the heel in place.
Return slowly without moving the whole leg.
Complete the set, then switch the working foot.
description: One forefoot turns outward against a band anchored by the other foot. The outer lower-leg muscles control the small ankle and foot movement.

name: Seated Band Ankle Plantar Flexion
instructions: Sit on a stable seat and loop a band around the ball of one foot.
Hold the band ends in your hands and extend that foot slightly in front of you.
Keep the lower leg steady as you point the foot away against the band.
Return slowly, allowing the toes to come back toward the shin.
Repeat before changing feet.
description: The foot points downward against a hand-held band while seated. The calf muscles produce ankle plantar flexion.

name: Seated Band Ankle Eversion
instructions: Sit with both feet on the floor and loop a band around the front of the working foot.
Pass the band beneath the other foot to anchor it and hold the free end steady.
Keep the working heel in place as you turn the front of the foot outward against the band.
Return slowly without turning the knee or lifting the thigh.
Complete the set, then change feet.
description: The working foot turns outward against a band anchored under the other foot. The peroneal muscles along the outer lower leg resist the band.

name: Seated Band Ankle Inversion
instructions: Sit with the working heel on the floor and cross the other lower leg in front of it.
Loop a band around the working forefoot, route it around the front foot as an outside anchor and hold the free end.
Keep the shin steady as you turn the sole inward against the band.
Return slowly through the same small range.
Complete the set and reverse the crossed-leg setup to work the other foot.
description: The working foot turns inward against a band that pulls from its outer side. The tibialis posterior and tibialis anterior contribute to ankle inversion.

name: Standing Chin Tuck
instructions: Stand upright with your eyes forward and shoulders relaxed.
Slide your head straight backward, gently drawing your chin in without looking up or down.
Pause with the back of your neck long and your jaw relaxed.
Return your head to its starting position and repeat.
description: The head glides backward over the torso while the gaze stays level. This small controlled movement works the deep neck muscles.

name: Wall Chin Tuck with Finger Guidance
instructions: Stand with your upper back near a wall and look straight ahead.
Place your fingertips lightly on your chin.
Use gentle finger guidance to slide your head backward toward the wall without tilting it up or down.
Pause with your shoulders relaxed, then release to the starting position.
description: Light finger pressure guides the head backward toward a wall. The neck stays long and the eyes remain level during the chin tuck.

name: Quick-Feet Run in Place
instructions: Stand with your knees softly bent and elbows beside your body.
Take very short, quick alternating steps in place.
Keep the contacts light and your hips at a steady height.
Move your arms opposite your legs and maintain a rhythm you can control.
Slow the steps gradually to finish.
description: Short rapid steps keep the body nearly in place while the arms move in opposition. The repeated stepping provides cardiovascular work.

name: Prancing Running Drill
instructions: Start upright with your elbows bent in a running position.
Push through one forefoot into a small springing step while the opposite leg moves forward.
Land lightly and transfer into the next step on the other foot.
Swing the arms opposite the legs and keep the steps low and rhythmic.
Continue alternating for your planned distance or duration.
description: Light springing steps alternate between the legs with a running arm swing. The calves contribute to the push-off while the repeated movement trains coordination and cardiovascular fitness.

name: Alternating Zigzag Bounds Through Cones
instructions: Set out a line of small cones with enough space to move diagonally between them.
Begin beside the first cone in a soft-kneed athletic stance.
Push off one foot and move diagonally forward to land on the opposite foot on the other side of the line.
Bend the landing ankle, knee and hip to absorb the contact.
Push off again toward the next opening and continue alternating feet through the zigzag.
Slow down after the last cone and reset.
description: Diagonal bounds alternate single-foot contacts while traveling through a line of cones. The calves, quadriceps and glutes produce the push-offs and absorb the landings.

name: Skipping
instructions: Stand tall with your elbows bent and feet under your hips.
Step onto one foot and make a small hop on that foot while lifting the opposite knee.
Land on the hopping foot, then step onto the other foot.
Hop on the new support foot and lift the opposite knee.
Continue the alternating step-and-hop rhythm with opposite arm swings.
description: A repeated step and hop alternates the supporting leg while the opposite knee rises. Skipping combines a light bouncing gait with cardiovascular work.

name: Strongman Fingal's Finger Lift
instructions: Stand at the free end of the hinged pole with your feet planted and both hands gripping beneath its end.
Bend your knees and hips, then extend your legs to lift the pole from the ground.
Step forward as the end rises, changing from an underhand lifting grip to a pushing position.
Move your hands along the pole and push it toward an upright position without tipping it beyond vertical.
Reverse the movement under control, stepping back and lowering the free end to the ground.
Let the pole settle before resetting your grip for the next repetition.
description: Lift a hinged strongman pole from the ground toward vertical, then lower it back to the starting side. The legs and hips begin the lift before the shoulders and arms push it higher.

name: Strongman Overhead Keg Toss
instructions: Stand with a clear landing area around and behind you and grip the keg securely with both hands.
Bend your knees and hips to lower the keg between your legs.
Drive through your feet and extend your hips and knees to send the keg upward.
Continue the arm swing overhead and release the keg upward and away from your body.
Stay clear of its flight and landing, then retrieve it only after it has settled.
description: A strong hip and leg drive launches a keg overhead. The glutes and legs generate the initial force while the shoulders guide the release.

name: Barbell Clean, Front Squat and Press Complex
instructions: Stand over the barbell with feet under your hips and grip it just outside your legs.
Extend your legs and hips to clean the bar to the fronts of your shoulders, turning your elbows forward underneath it.
Keep the bar at the shoulders as you perform a front squat, then stand upright.
Press the bar overhead until both arms are extended.
Lower the bar carefully behind your head toward your upper back, then press it overhead again.
Lower the bar to the front of your shoulders and guide it down to the floor.
Reset your stance and grip before repeating the complete sequence.
description: A clean and front squat lead into two overhead presses, with an upper-back lowering phase between them. This advanced sequence combines lower-body lifting with shoulder and arm pressing.

name: Strongman Car Flip
instructions: Position yourself at the side of the prepared car-flip implement and secure both hands beneath its lifting edge.
Bend your knees and hips while keeping your back steady.
Extend your legs and hips to raise that side of the car.
As it rises, step closer and change your hands into a pushing position.
Push the car beyond its balance point and move clear of its landing path.
Wait until the implement has settled before resetting.
description: One side of a car is lifted and pushed over in a strongman flip. The legs and hips start the lift, followed by an upper-body push.

name: Double-Under Jump Rope
instructions: Hold the rope handles beside your hips and start with the rope behind your feet.
Swing the rope with your wrists and jump vertically from both feet.
Turn the rope quickly enough to pass beneath your feet twice before you land.
Keep your body tall and land softly with your knees slightly bent.
Continue with a controlled rhythm, resetting if you miss the rope.
description: The rope makes two revolutions during each two-foot jump. The calves and coordinated wrist action support this cardiovascular skipping drill.

name: Dumbbell Push-Up, Row, Clean and Press Complex
instructions: Place two stable dumbbells on the floor and hold their handles in a high plank with your feet spread for balance.
Perform a push-up, then row one dumbbell toward your ribs and place it back down.
Perform another push-up, then row the other dumbbell and return it to the floor.
Bring your feet forward and stand with both dumbbells hanging beside your thighs.
Dip through your hips and knees, then clean the dumbbells to your shoulders and receive them in a squat.
Stand from the squat and press both dumbbells overhead.
Lower the weights with control, place them on the floor and return your feet to the plank to begin again.
description: Two push-up and row combinations lead into a dumbbell clean, squat and overhead press. The sequence combines chest, back, leg and shoulder work while the abdomen stabilizes the transitions.
aliases: Dumbbell Complex Push Up Row Clean and Press

name: Box Jump-Over with Turns
instructions: Stand facing a stable plyometric box with your feet about hip-width apart.
Bend your knees and hips and swing your arms back.
Jump onto the box with both feet, turning about a quarter-turn as you land in a controlled crouch.
Jump off the far side and turn another quarter-turn in the same direction to face back toward the box.
Land with bent knees and hips, then regain your balance before repeating.
description: A jump onto the box includes a quarter-turn, followed by another turning jump to the floor on the far side. The quadriceps and glutes power the jumps and control the landings.

name: Standing Band Pallof Press
instructions: Anchor a band at chest height and stand sideways to it with your feet planted apart.
Hold the band with both hands at your chest and gently tighten your abdomen.
Press your hands straight forward while resisting the band pulling your torso toward the anchor.
Draw your hands back to your chest without turning your shoulders or hips.
Complete the set, then turn around to face the opposite direction and repeat.
description: The arms press forward while the trunk resists rotation toward a side anchor. The abs and obliques keep the torso facing ahead.

name: Band Lateral Shuffle
instructions: Place a loop band around your ankles and stand with your feet apart.
Bend your knees and hips slightly into an athletic stance.
Step sideways with one foot, then bring the other foot after it without allowing the band to go slack.
Keep your knees pointing with your toes and your hips at a steady height.
Continue for several steps, then reverse direction.
description: Sideways steps keep tension in a band around the ankles. The gluteus medius and other hip muscles control the legs while the quadriceps maintain the bent-knee stance.

name: Broad Jump to Vertical Jump
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and arms relaxed.
Bend your hips and knees while swinging your arms behind you.
Swing the arms forward and jump ahead from both feet.
Land softly with both feet and bend your knees to absorb the impact.
Use that bend to spring straight upward into a vertical jump.
Land again with control and reset before repeating.
description: A forward broad jump flows into a vertical jump after landing. The quadriceps, glutes and calves generate the takeoffs and manage both landings.

name: Medicine Ball Overhead Partner Throw
instructions: Stand facing a prepared partner and hold a medicine ball in both hands near your chest.
Raise the ball above and slightly behind your head while keeping your torso controlled.
Extend your arms forward to throw the ball to your partner.
Finish with your hands reaching forward and your feet balanced.
Receive the return with bent elbows, bring the ball back toward your chest and reset.
description: The ball is lifted behind the head and thrown forward to a partner, who returns it. The triceps and shoulders produce the overhead throwing action.

name: Two-Hand Kettlebell Overhead Carry
instructions: Hold a kettlebell securely in both hands and raise it overhead with both arms extended.
Keep your abdomen gently tightened and the weight balanced above you.
Walk forward with short controlled steps while keeping your torso tall.
Avoid letting the kettlebell drift forward or your lower back arch.
Stop walking before lowering the kettlebell carefully to your chest and then down.
description: Both hands support one kettlebell overhead while the legs alternate through a walk. The shoulders sustain the load and the abs control the trunk.

name: Single-Leg Broad Jump
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other foot clear of the floor.
Bend the supporting knee and hip while swinging your arms back.
Drive through that foot and swing the arms forward to jump ahead.
Land on the same foot with the knee and hip bent to absorb the contact.
Regain balance before repeating, then change legs.
description: A forward jump takes off and lands on the same leg. The quadriceps, glutes and calves propel the body and control the landing.

name: Medicine Ball Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Hold a medicine ball close to your chest with both hands.
Gently tighten your abdomen and curl your shoulders and upper back from the floor.
Keep the ball close without pushing it forward or pulling your neck.
Lower your upper back slowly and repeat.
description: A medicine ball held near the chest adds resistance to a short floor crunch. The abs curl the upper torso while the feet stay planted.

name: Single-Leg Vertical Jump
instructions: Stand on one foot with the other leg free and your arms ready to swing.
Bend the supporting hip and knee to prepare for the jump.
Swing your arms upward and drive through the standing foot to jump vertically.
Lift the free knee as you rise, then land on the same support foot.
Bend the hip and knee to absorb the landing and regain balance before repeating.
Complete the set and switch legs.
description: One leg powers a vertical jump and accepts the landing while the other knee rises. The quadriceps, glutes and calves contribute to the takeoff and landing control.

name: Straight-Leg Heel Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended, heels on the floor and arms folded across your chest.
Gently tighten your abdomen and press both heels into the floor.
Lift your hips until your torso and legs form a long line without arching your back.
Keep the knees nearly straight as you pause briefly.
Lower your hips slowly and repeat.
description: The heels remain far from the hips during this long-lever bridge. The hamstrings and glutes raise the pelvis while the upper back stays on the floor.

name: Single-Leg Step-Down Squat
instructions: Stand on a stable step with one foot near its edge and the other foot free in front.
Keep your hips level as you bend the supporting knee and hip.
Lower until the free heel lightly reaches the floor without shifting your weight onto it.
Press through the foot on the step to return upright.
Repeat slowly, then change legs.
description: One leg lowers the body from a step while the other heel reaches toward the floor. The working quadriceps and glutes control the descent and return.

name: Lateral Shuffle
instructions: Start in a low athletic stance with your knees bent and feet apart.
Push off one foot and step sideways with the other.
Bring the trailing foot after it without crossing your feet.
Take several quick steps, then plant the outside foot and reverse direction.
Keep your hips low and your chest facing forward throughout.
description: Quick sideways steps alternate directions from a bent-knee stance. The legs produce continuous lateral movement for cardiovascular and coordination work.

name: Backward Running
instructions: Check that the path behind you is clear and start standing upright.
Take short alternating steps backward with your knees softly bent.
Swing your arms opposite your legs and keep your torso steady.
Maintain a controlled pace and recheck your path as needed.
Slow down and stop before turning to move in a new direction.
description: Short running steps travel backward while the arms move opposite the legs. The alternating gait provides cardiovascular work with a different direction of travel.
